limitations: 功能摘要根据作者固定版本材料归纳，不是逐字引文或独立效果验证。

limitations: 核根/实现子包manifest与补丁、原生入口、transport真实caller/owner/fallback、目录判定、消息/工具/请求形状、chat/responses SDK调用、预算/首交付/终态/watchdog、relay、IP池装配/installer、设置桥与客户端调用。未全审池全部协议解析器/节点/准入分支、legacy Go sidecar、所有UI、外部SDK实现及实际宿主/发布包；未执行目标代码或网络探测。
只执行本工程的统计和结构验证；没有执行目标插件、测试、安装或真实宿主验收。
GitHub/npm 活跃度只作采集背景，未核实独立用户采用或同条件收益对照。

findings.text: 已有DSH用户在同一会话进行匿名文本/工具任务，验收应看真实产物、结果续接与终态；目录及ready不是任务成功。见[Q01](#research-q01)。
注册原生adapter、目录判定、Context/工具别名转换、两条SDK协议及usage/finish形成源码调用链；是否接入Bun relay取决于入口transport及共享fetch owner，首内容前有内部恢复，实际工具循环属于宿主。见[Q02](#research-q02)、[Q03](#research-q03)。

核根/实现子包manifest与补丁、原生入口、transport真实caller/owner/fallback、目录判定、消息/工具/请求形状、chat/responses SDK调用、预算/首交付/终态/watchdog、relay、IP池装配/installer、设置桥与客户端调用。未全审池全部协议解析器/节点/准入分支、legacy Go sidecar、所有UI、外部SDK实现及实际宿主/发布包；未执行目标代码或网络探测。
根private dsh-plugin-adapter无自身version；实现子包声明@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-adapter0.6.0、MIT、Node>=20、fork归属，lib需构建。根^0.3.4与本源码未绑定，实际发布/安装及依赖engine未验，见[Q01](#research-q01)。
维护负担取决于匿名协议/目录漂移、真实出口和共享网络退出，而非只取决于模型名价格；内部重试与后台probe可能增加请求。四阶段明细集中于[Q04](#research-q04)，没有可报告的净节省实测。
观察：先核根真实包和退出恢复，再做一项可验文本/工具任务；严格出站、结果归属或共享网络未达标即停新请求并回退，见[Q06](#research-q06)。
当前价值在会话接入与故障边界可检查；是否胜过现成provider，应按完成的工具任务和纠错工时检验。效果表及不能确定项见[Q04](#research-q04)，真实路径反例见[Q05](#research-q05)。
可借鉴输出预算、工具ID/别名、无终态报错和首交付后不重放；不能照搬CLI指纹、将watchdog当上游取消，或以状态卡/恢复日志代替真实路径和owner恢复。见[Q02](#research-q02)、[Q03](#research-q03)。
将匿名目录、消息/工具事件、预算夹紧和故障终态接到宿主模型契约；首交付后不再重放有可检查边界，但不是插件独立实现Agent循环或已验证服务保障。见[Q02](#research-q02)。
根^0.3.4未锁定到所审子包0.6.0；入口池开时relay句柄未接Zen，池关仍受fetch owner与失败ambient回落约束，installer在setter返回void时没有保存/恢复旧slot。条件源码缺口未作为真实宿主故障，产物、实际出口与退出仍是采用门槛。见[Q01](#research-q01)、[Q03](#research-q03)。
在已有诊断上绑定一次调用的真实产物/路径、首交付、终态与释放确认，先用匿名失败任务对照原生日志和简单修补；无定位/纠错收益就不产品化。尚未实现或验证，见[Q05](#research-q05)。
实际产物、宿主注册接口和匿名上游是前提，Bun/代理/池与sing-box按真实路径分支判断。子包源码不能替代npm包或当前宿主兼容验收；完整条件表见[Q04](#research-q04)。

technical.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)有fork后的独立接线，novelty9高于无增量0，成熟SDK/协议基础不达新机制18。[Q02](#research-q02)双协议、别名/终态/首交付边界可解释，mechanism23超过单接口15，超时/退出未闭环不30。事件与错误契约可迁移10超过本地5，指纹和匿名通道强绑定不15；省搬会话有简化4，但多层传输/进程与恢复责任不8。[Q03](#research-q03)条件缺口不按已复现故障扩大。

business.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)原生会话是单点便利workflow9，未形成新业务闭环不18；[Q02](#research-q02)有实际模型响应接线delivery8，但产物与真实任务/服务保障不足15。DSH接入有reach5，需维护匿名通道且无新人群证据不10；匿名入口有成本控制意图economics4超过纯展示0，[Q04](#research-q04)无账单、质量和维护净收益不8。未把候选路径凭据计为现有创新。

recommendation.reason: 更适合已有DSH、能独立核对构建产物与出站策略的人，在隔离profile里观察匿名文本/工具会话的接入价值。固定源码串起原生provider和可分类终态，但根安装未绑定所审子包、默认relay可另起Bun且卸载恢复有条件缺口，尚不足作为主力长期免费服务。若不能确认真实版本、已交付工具不被重放和停用后的全局网络恢复，就停止接入并核对在途请求，回到现有provider。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)同会话文本/工具任务具体，超过泛便利15；真实需求频率/稳定服务未验不30。

advantage.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)目录/事件/终态接线超过纯声明6；相对现有provider或CLI未验端到端优势不19。

evidence.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)不是仅因未运行降分：实际根安装物与所审子包无锁定证明，核心交付物尚未对应，不达完整源码绑定交付的13；已有固定核心链而非无材料0。

cost.rationale: [Q03](#research-q03)额外进程/出站和共享slot退出责任重于简单配置，不达10；有明确条件与清理代码并非全未知0，四阶段负担见[Q04](#research-q04)。

publication.summaries.text: 以原生provider接入匿名Zen模型，含目录、消息/工具流适配及可选relay/IP池；根产物绑定待核。

items.界面: Web插件页注册IP池卡，使用configForms保存设置，轮询本机桥接状态并触发probe。
items.Host 路由: loopback/同源检查下的池status/models/probe POST；probe有实际网络和补池副作用。
items.后台: 目录刷新、按需Bun relay及可选池补源/订阅/探测；原生模型适配依赖宿主实际工具执行。

publication.capabilities.table:
| 能力 | 主要用途 | 使用条件与边界 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 原生模型适配 | 匿名文本、工具事件/结果续接与终态 | 实际包与本源码需绑定，工具执行/循环属于宿主 |
| 目录与预算 | 免费判定、静态fallback和输出夹紧 | 标签/目录不证明活模型或长期免费 |
| 分层传输 | Bun relay、Node与可选池 | 池开入口未接relay，池关需槽owner允许且可fallback ambient；严格策略另验 |
| 池设置/诊断 | Web卡、状态/模型/探测POST和live apply | 本机/同源guard，probe有副作用；状态不是任务就绪 |

      "path": "README.md",
      "content": "<div align=\"center\">\n\n# dsh-plugin-adapter\n\n**Free OpenCode Zen models, natively inside DSH (DeepSeek Harness).**\n\nNo API key. No registration. No extra process.\n\n[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)\n[![node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%E2%89%A520-brightgreen)](https://nodejs.org)\n[![DeepSeek Harness](https://img.shields.io/badge/DeepSeek%20Harness-plugin-blue)](https://github.com/1624318455/dsh-plugin-adapter)\n\n<div>\n  <a href=\"LICENSE\"><img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green\" alt=\"license\"></a>\n  <a href=\"https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin\"><img src=\"https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/badge.svg\" alt=\"Awesome\"></a>\n  <a href=\"https://nodejs.org\"><img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/node-20%2B-blue\" alt=\"node\"></a>\n  <a href=\"packages/plugin/test\"><img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-162%20passed-success\" alt=\"tests\"></a>\n  <a href=\"https://github.com/1624318455/dsh-plugin-adapter\"><img src=\"https://img.shields.io/github/stars/1624318455/dsh-plugin-adapter\" alt=\"stars\"></a>\n  <a href=\"https://github.com/1624318455/dsh-plugin-adapter/commits/master\"><img src=\"https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/1624318455/dsh-plugin-adapter\" alt=\"last commit\"></a>\n</div>\n\nEnglish | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)\n\n</div>\n\n---\n\ndsh-plugin-adapter registers a native DSH `LlmAdapter` that streams directly from\n[OpenCode Zen](https://opencode.ai/zen)'s **anonymous free lane** — the same\nmodels OpenCode's own CLI uses without an account, served to your DSH model\npicker as a regular provider called `zen-free` (`opencode2dsh` stays\nregistered as a legacy alias so old sessions keep working).\n\nRequests leave your machine looking exactly like traffic from the OpenCode\nCLI (same user agent, same correlation headers), and the model catalog stays\nfresh through a three-tier fallback chain. There is nothing to log into and\nnothing to host.\n\n## Highlights\n\n- **Zero credential, zero setup** — the anonymous lane needs no key; install, restart, chat\n- **Native adapter, no sidecar** — one npm package, no child process, no binary, no local port (the legacy Go sidecar is not part of the published package; see `legacy/`)\n- **CLI-identical disguise** — requests carry the OpenCode CLI user agent and its session/request/project header set, derived per conversation\n- **Selectable thinking levels** — reasoning-capable free models expose an effort picker in DSH's model selector (declared ladders where the model metadata provides them, Off/Minimal/Low/Medium/High otherwise); Off sends `reasoning_effort: \"none\"` upstream to actually stop thinking, and no selection keeps the provider default\n- **Live catalog with a fallback chain** — live upstream list ∩ free verdict (models.dev price 0, or a `-free` id the lane itself serves free), falling back to offline cache and a verified static list\n- **Self-healing** — fast startup retries, periodic refresh, and a written health snapshot for diagnostics\n- **Proper error surfaces** — upstream failures (rate limit, auth, timeout, transport) arrive in DSH as classified finish reasons, and retries stay owned by DSH\n\n## Install\n\n**From the plugin market** (recommended, once listed):\nin DSH open **Settings → Plugin Market**, search `dsh-plugin-adapter`,\none-click install.\n\n**From GitHub**:\n\n```sh\ndsh plugin --profile web add github:1624318455/dsh-plugin-adapter\n```\n\n**From npm**:\n\n```sh\ndsh plugin --profile web add @memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-adapter\n```\n\n**From source** (build the tarball yourself):\n\n```sh\ngit clone https://github.com/1624318455/dsh-plugin-adapter.git\ncd dsh-plugin-adapter/packages/plugin\npnpm install && pnpm pack\ndsh plugin --profile web add ./memef1f1y-dsh-plugin-adapter-<version>.tgz\n```\n\n**Verify**: restart `dsh web`, open the model picker, and pick a model from\nthe **zen-free** group.\n\nRequires DSH (DeepSeek Harness) with a web profile; Node.js ≥ 20 (already\npresent if DSH runs); outbound HTTPS to `opencode.ai` and `models.dev`.\n\n## Configuration\n\nDefaults work out of the box. Override via the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:\n\n```yaml\n- id: dsh-plugin-adapter\n  name: '@memef1f1y/dsh-plugin-adapter'\n  config:\n    mode: adapter        # adapter (default) | sidecar\n    providerId: zen-free\n    refreshSeconds: 300  # catalog refresh cadence\n```\n\n> **Upgrading from ≤ 0.3.x**: the plugin id changed from `opencode2dsh` to\n> `dsh-plugin-adapter` in 0.4.0. DSH attaches the config block to the plugin\n> by that id, so rename the `- id:` line in your live `cordis.patch.yml` in\n> the same step — otherwise the config (e.g. a pinned `gatewaySession`) is\n> silently dropped. The data directory moved with it (`~/.opencode2dsh` →\n> `~/.dsh-plugin-adapter`): the plugin copies the old one over on first\n> start and parks it as `~/.opencode2dsh.bak-<date>`, which you can delete\n> once the new setup works.\n\n| Option | Default | Description |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `mode` | `adapter` | `adapter`: native LlmAdapter streaming straight from Zen. `sidecar`: legacy local-agent mode, not bundled — build the agent from `legacy/agent` and pass `agentPath`. |\n| `providerId` | `zen-free` | Provider name shown in DSH (`opencode2dsh` stays registered as a legacy alias). |\n| `refreshSeconds` | `300` | Live catalog refresh interval. Pricing metadata refreshes every 24 h. |\n| `gatewaySession` | — | Fixed session id sent as `x-opencode-session` for every request. **Leave unset unless you need the escape hatch**: the Zen free lane meters its quota per *session id*, so a pinned id makes every conversation share one bucket (one 429 then breaks the whole app until the id changes). Unpinned, the adapter derives a canonical id per conversation from its first user turn — stable across turns, distinct per conversation, so each conversation gets its own quota pool. Escape hatch for a conversation stuck on a sick upstream replica: pin a live OpenCode CLI session id here and restart DSH. |\n| `watchdog.firstEventMs` | `60000` | Time-to-first-token budget. The Zen lane holds the response head back until the upstream emits its first token, so this window is about a slow first answer, not a dead exit. |\n| `watchdog.reasoningFirstEventMs` | `90000` | Same budget for reasoning models (they compose longer before the first token). |\n| `watchdog.bodyIdleMs` | `120000` | Body-silence budget after content started flowing (300 s for Responses models). |\n| `contextWindow` | — | Cap for the context window the adapter advertises to DSH (tokens). DSH compacts against the window the provider reports, and the free models declare **1,000,000** — so a long session never compacts and every turn re-sends the whole growing surface (measured: 404 K surface tokens, 205 K read back from the prompt cache per step). Capping it (e.g. `262144`, the free lane's real window) makes DSH compact earlier: smaller prompts, faster first token, less quota burnt. Unset = advertise the model's own window. **The advertised output limit follows this window**: it is `min(model limit, window / 4)`, because DSH's compactor reserves the request's `maxTokens` *inside* the window (`messageBudget = contextWindow - maxTokens`) and silently skips compaction when that budget is not positive. |\n| `transport.proxyUrl` | — | Proxy URI for the Zen lane, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:10808`. Gives the lane its own dispatcher with a **fresh CONNECT tunnel per request**, so a proxy that silently closed the previous tunnel cannot kill the turn with `UND_ERR_SOCKET` / `ECONNRESET`. Other hosts keep the ambient dispatcher. |\n| `transport.noReuse` | `true` | Set `false` to keep connection reuse on the Zen lane. |\n| `agentPath` | auto-resolved | Sidecar only: path to the agent binary. |\n| `agentArgs` | — | Sidecar only: extra CLI args for the agent. |\n| `restartDelayMs` / `restartMaxDelayMs` / `maxConsecutiveCrashes` | `1000` / `60000` / `5` | Sidecar only: restart backoff and circuit breaker. |\n\n## How it works\n\n```\nDSH session\n   │  harness chunks (block-start / text-delta / usage / finish …)\n   ▼\nZenAdapter (registered LlmAdapter)\n   │  pi-ai openai-completions stream\n   ▼\nhttps://opencode.ai/zen/v1        ← Authorization: Bearer public\n   with CLI-identical headers:\n     user-agent: opencode/…\n     x-opencode-client, x-opencode-session, x-session-affinity,\n     X-Session-Id, x-opencode-request, x-opencode-project\n```\n\n- **Session correlation** — session/project ids are SHA-256 derived from the\n  conversation's first user turn (stable per conversation, non-reversible),\n  and each request gets a fresh random id, mirroring the CLI.\n- **Catalog fallback chain** — S1: live `GET /v1/models`; S2: models.dev\n  pricing metadata decides \"free\"; S3: a compile-time verified static list.\n  A disk cache (~7-day TTL) covers upstream outages.\n- **Resilience** — the adapter registers immediately at startup; if the first\n  catalog fetch races your network (VPN/TUN reconnects, DNS), the plugin\n  retries on a short cadence (~1 min) before settling into the periodic\n  refresh.\n- **Sidecar mode** (`mode: sidecar`, legacy) — spawns a local Go agent (a\n  single-tenant port of [opencode2api](https://github.com/jasonxu114514/opencode2api))\n  on `127.0.0.1:<random>`, token-authenticated, and registers a standard\n  `llm-pi-ai` route. **Not part of the published package**; build it from\n  `legacy/agent` (`go build ./cmd/agent`) and point `agentPath` at the binary.\n\n## Gateway compatibility (Zen gate tracking)\n\nZen's free lane gates third-party clients and moves models between APIs\nwithout notice. Two mechanisms matter here:\n\n- **Canonical sessions (upstream)** — the gateway only serves\n  `x-opencode-session` ids shaped `ses_<12 hex><14 base62>`; every identity\n  is hashed into that shape, so plain DSH conversations pass with no setup.\n- **Responses-only models (this fork)** — `muse-spark-*` return a bare 500 on\n  `/chat/completions` but 200 on `/responses`. The adapter routes them to\n  pi-ai `openai-responses` (wider 300 s body-idle watchdog for bursty\n  reasoning); everything else stays on `openai-completions`.\n\n## Health & troubleshooting\n\nThe plugin writes a health snapshot after every refresh round:\n\n```\n~/.dsh-plugin-adapter/adapter-status.json\n```\n\n```json\n{\n  \"status\": \"ready\",\n  \"total\": 64,\n  \"exposed\": 9,\n  \"lastError\": \"\",\n  \"writtenAt\": \"2026-08-29T07:01:54.915Z\"\n}\n```\n\n| Symptom | Likely cause & fix |\n| --- | --- |\n| Boot screen shows `Failed to load plugins … list slot \"settings.plugin.item\" requires options.id` | Your DSH is too old (≤ 0.1.0-rc.6): the settings-slot contract predates the plugin 0.3.0 browser half. Upgrade DSH to ≥ 0.1.0-rc.7 (latest recommended). Plugin ≥ 0.3.1 registers in either slot shape, so on old DSH you lose at most the settings card — model routing is unaffected. |\n| Only 3 models | Startup fetch raced your network; retries land within ~1 min. Check `adapter-status.json` for `lastError`. |\n| `lastError: \"fetch failed\"` persisting | Outbound HTTPS to `opencode.ai` blocked; check proxy/VPN rules. |\n| Rate-limit errors in chat | The anonymous lane is quota-per-IP; switch network node or wait. |\n| `500` on `muse-spark-*` via chat | Responses-only model; this fork routes it to `/responses` automatically. |\n| `403 FreeTierError: free tier can only be used from within OpenCode` | Update past 0.3.2 (canonical sessions + gate-tools body shaping); non-streaming probes always 403 — diagnose with `stream:true`. |\n| `stream body idle timeout` on reasoning models | Bursty chain-of-thought tripped the 120 s watchdog; this fork uses 300 s for Responses models. |\n| `first stream event timeout` | A **time-to-first-token** timeout, not a dead exit: the Zen lane holds the response head back until the upstream emits its first token, so a slow first answer used to be reported as a silent exit. The window is 60 s (90 s for reasoning models) and configurable via `watchdog.*`; the IP pool rotates the exit when one is available. |\n| Old session fails every turn, new sessions work | That conversation's session is pinned to a sick upstream replica — see `gatewaySession` above. |\n| `429 … \"Upstream request failed: Endpoint is unavailable.\"` | The gateway's backing model instance is down — **not** a quota error and not exit-specific. The adapter re-rolls the session id once (the lane pins an instance per session), which moves the request to another instance. |\n| `Request timed out.` | The OpenAI SDK's request bound fired before any response header. The adapter now passes an explicit bound (`watchdog` window + 30 s) so a wedged upstream cannot hang for the SDK's 10-minute default, and the watchdog's diagnostic message wins instead of this bare one. |\n| `400 … requires adaptive thinking; reasoning effort none is not allowed` | The model refuses to stop thinking (`minimax-m3.1*`). Asking for `off` is mapped to the cheapest accepted level (`low`) instead of failing the turn. |\n| Connection error to `127.0.0.1:*` | A stale sidecar route shadows the adapter; plugin ≥ 0.2.1 removes it at startup. |\n| Install fails with `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS` | A transitive dependency of `pi-ai` (`@google/genai`, `protobufjs`) has build scripts that are not needed at runtime. Approve-or-decline them via the plugin market, or set both to `false` under `allowBuilds:` in the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. |\n\n## Security\n\n- No secrets involved: the anonymous lane's key is the literal string `public`; nothing is stored, nothing telemetry.\n- Install paths restricted to `lib/` only; no build scripts run from dependencies.\n- All requests go directly from your machine to `opencode.ai` / `models.dev`.\n\n## Development\n\n```sh\ngit clone https://github.com/1624318455/dsh-plugin-adapter.git\ncd dsh-plugin-adapter/packages/plugin\npnpm install\npnpm typecheck && pnpm test\npnpm build                    # bundle to lib/\n```\n\nThe legacy Go sidecar lives in `legacy/agent` (`go test ./...`). Architecture\nnotes and the porting record live in `docs/`.\n\nReleasing: push a `v*` tag (the tag must equal the `version` in\n`packages/plugin/package.json`). The `publish` workflow tests on Node 22/24 and\nthen publishes `packages/plugin` to npm with provenance through npm's Trusted\nPublisher (GitHub Actions OIDC, no long-lived token). Locally, `pnpm pack` in\n`packages/plugin` still works (prepack builds and syncs the docs).\n\n## Acknowledgments\n\n- [opencode2dsh](https://github.com/FishBottle7/opencode2dsh) by\n  [FishBottle7](https://github.com/FishBottle7) — this project is a maintained\n  fork of it; the adapter, catalog and IP-pool design originate there.\n- [**opencode2api**](https://github.com/jasonxu114514/opencode2api) by\n  [@jasonxu114514](https://github.com/jasonxu114514) — the legacy Go sidecar\n  in `legacy/agent` is a port of its anonymous-lane implementation, and the\n  catalog fallback chain and request-disguise details are derived from it.\n  This project stands on its shoulders.\n- [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) — for running the free anonymous Zen lane.\n- [@earendil-works/pi-ai](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@earendil-works/pi-ai) — the wire layer used by adapter mode.\n- [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh) and the\n  [dsh-market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) community.\n\n## Friends\n\n<div align=\"center\">\n\n**[LinuxDo](https://linux.do)** — 新的理想型社区 / a new ideal community\n\n</div>\n\n## License\n\n[MIT](./LICENSE) © FishBottle7\n"

''} ${provider.name ?? ZEN_BASE_URL\n    this.#metadataUrl = options.metadataUrl ?? 'https://models.dev/api.json'\n    this.#fetch = options.fetchImpl ?? fetch\n    this.#now = options.now ??       "content": "/**\n * Zen-lane transport hardening.\n *\n * WHY (live-observed 2026-10-21): the ambient dispatcher\n * (dsh-plugin-proxy's `EnvHttpProxyAgent`) keeps the proxy-side CONNECT\n * tunnel alive between requests. Clash/v2rayN silently close idle tunnels,\n * and the NEXT request on the dead tunnel dies with `UND_ERR_SOCKET`\n * (wrote 905 bytes, read 0) or `ECONNRESET` instead of opening a fresh\n * CONNECT. Measured through the default agent: 2 of 12 requests failed that\n * way; with `pipelining: 0` (fresh tunnel per request) the same probe\n * produced 0 socket errors.\n *\n * WHAT: the Zen lane gets its OWN dispatcher, so the fix does not depend on\n * the proxy plugin's build. The hardened dispatcher is only used for the\n * Zen host; every other request keeps the ambient path (the proxy plugin\n * still owns the global dispatcher for the rest of the process).\n *\n * MECHANICS: pi-ai talks to the upstream through the OpenAI SDK, which\n * calls `globalThis.fetch`. Node's built-in fetch REJECTS a dispatcher\n * instance that comes from another undici module copy\n * (`UND_ERR_INVALID_ARG`, measured), so the hardened path calls THIS\n * module's `undici.fetch` with `dispatcher` in the init — that is the same\n * trick the IP-pool installer uses (pool/installer.ts:124-129).\n *\n * FAIL-SAFE: the hardened path must never be the reason the lane dies. Empty = no hardening. */\n  proxyUrl?: string\n  /**\n   * Force a fresh CONNECT tunnel per request (default true). '').trim()\n  if (value === '') return null\n  let parsed: URL\n  try {\n    parsed = new URL(value)\n  } catch {\n    return null\n  }\n  if (parsed.protocol !== 'http:' && parsed.protocol !== 'https:') return null\n  return parsed.toString()\n}\n\n/** The host part of the request URL we reroute (accepts \"host:port\"). */\nfunction normalizeHost(raw: string | undefined): string {\n  const value = (raw ?? '').trim()\n  const candidate = value === ''\n    ? ZEN_BASE_URL\n    : /^[a-z0-9+.-]+:\\/\\//i.test(value) ? value : `http://${value}`\n  try {\n    return new URL(candidate).host\n  } catch {\n    return new URL(ZEN_BASE_URL).host\n  }\n}\n\n/** Extract the request URL from the shapes fetch accepts. */\nfunction requestUrl(input: unknown): URL | null {\n  try {\n    if (typeof input === 'string') return new URL(input)\n    if (input instanceof URL) return input\n    const maybe = input as { url?: unknown; href?: unknown }\n    if (typeof maybe?.url === 'string') return new URL(maybe.url)\n    if (typeof maybe?.href === 'string') return new URL(maybe.href)\n  } catch {\n    return null\n  }\n  return null\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the Zen-lane transport.       "content": "import { createProvider, type Api, type Context, type Model } from '@earendil-works/pi-ai'\nimport * as openaiCompletions from '@earendil-works/pi-ai/api/openai-completions'\nimport * as openaiResponses from '@earendil-works/pi-ai/api/openai-responses'\n\nimport { ModelCatalog, ZEN_BASE_URL, type ModelLimits } from './catalog.ts'\nimport { toStreamChunks, type HarnessChunk, type PiEvent } from './events.ts'\nimport { shapeChatBody, shapeResponsesBody, restoreToolName } from './fingerprint.ts'\nimport { canonicalSessionID, deriveRequestIDs, disguiseHeaders, randomID } from './ids.ts'\nimport { toPiContext, type HarnessGenerateOptions } from './messages.ts'\nimport type { ZenTransport } from './transport.ts'\nimport { routingContext, type RoutingContext } from '../pool/dispatcher.ts'\nimport { classifyStreamFailure, isCapacityFailure, isRegionBlocked, shouldRotate } from '../pool/rotate.ts'\n\n/**\n * The TS adapter: registers as a DSH LlmAdapter for the `zen-free` route\n * (plus the `opencode2dsh` legacy alias for pre-rename sessions)\n * and streams directly from the OpenCode Zen anonymous lane. The wire layer is\n * pi-ai's openai-completions implementation for most models (the same one DSH\n * uses for every OpenAI-compatible provider), plus pi-ai's openai-responses\n * for Responses-only models (muse-spark-*); this module adds the CLI disguise\n * headers, the derived session/request ids, and the free-model catalog.\n *\n * Adapter contract: dsh-llm LlmAdapter (providerInfo/listModels/resolveModel/\n * prepareCall/stream) — structural, no host import.\n */\n\nexport const PROVIDER_ID = 'zen-free'\n/** Legacy route id kept registered so existing sessions keep working. */\nexport const LEGACY_PROVIDER_ID = 'opencode2dsh'\n\nexport interface ZenModelInfo {\n  id: string\n  name: string\n  contextWindow: number\n  maxTokens: number\n}\n\nexport interface CatalogLike {\n  list(): string[]\n  decision(model: string): { allowed: boolean; source: string; known: boolean }\n  reasoningCapability(model: string): { reasoning: boolean; effortValues: string[] } | undefined\n  /** Optional: older fakes predate it — absence means \"metadata cannot speak\". */\n  modelLimits?(model: string): ModelLimits | undefined\n}\n\nconst DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW = 262144\nconst DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 32768\n\n/**\n * Output tokens the adapter may advertise for a window.\n *\n * The host reserves the advertised output limit INSIDE the advertised\n * context window: dsh-compaction-basic computes\n * `messageBudget = contextWindow - reservedCompletionTokens` (the reserve is\n * the request's `maxTokens`, i.e. exactly what we advertise) and throws a\n * target-pressure config error when that budget is not positive. The turn\n * then continues UNCOMPACTED (the error is only logged as a warning), so the\n * surface keeps growing until the lane cannot answer it any more.\n *\n * Measured 2026-10-22: minimax-m3.1-flash-free (1,000,000/512,000 in\n * models.dev) capped to a 131,072 window kept advertising 512,000 output\n * tokens, the reserve blew the message budget, compaction never ran, and the\n * session's surface reached 256,327 prompt tokens before the lane answered\n * with an empty length-stopped response.\n *\n * A quarter of the window keeps the envelope valid (the budget stays\n * positive even with the host's 64K headroom) and matches what the free\n * models actually produce (32K output).\n */\nexport function outputLimitFor(limits: ModelLimits): number {\n  const quarter = Math.floor(limits.contextWindow / 4)\n  return Math.max(1, Math.min(limits.maxTokens, quarter))\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve the advertised limits: per-model metadata/static first, generic\n * defaults last. `contextWindowCap` (config.contextWindow) trims the\n * advertised window: DSH compacts against the window the adapter reports, so\n * a 1M-token model never triggers compaction and every turn re-sends the\n * whole (growing) surface — the single biggest latency and quota lever.\n *\n * The output limit is then clamped into that window (see\n * {@link outputLimitFor}): an output limit that does not fit the window\n * breaks the host's compaction envelope.\n */\nfunction limitsFor(catalog: CatalogLike, model: string, contextWindowCap?: number): ModelLimits {\n  const limits = catalog.modelLimits?.(model) ?? { contextWindow: DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW, maxTokens: DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS }\n  const contextWindow =\n    contextWindowCap === undefined || contextWindowCap <= 0 ? limits.contextWindow : Math.min(limits.contextWindow, contextWindowCap)\n  return { contextWindow, maxTokens: outputLimitFor({ contextWindow, maxTokens: limits.maxTokens }) }\n}\n\n/**\n * Reasoning-effort vocabulary the adapter owns end to end (dsh-llm treats the\n * ids as opaque: whatever resolveModel advertises comes back on\n * GenerateOptions.reasoningEffort). The ladder mirrors pi-ai's ThinkingLevel\n * so selected levels pass through untouched; `off` is the only id that maps\n * to a different wire spelling.\n */\nexport const REASONING_EFFORT_LADDER = ['off', 'minimal', 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh', 'max'] as const\n\n/**\n * Levels offered for reasoning models whose metadata declares no ladder.\n * Fork: only levels verified live against the free lane (2026-09-19 probes:\n * low/medium/high/xhigh stream, `minimal` 403s, `off` maps to wire `none`\n * which muse-spark rejects — offering it would lie). Unset stays the default\n * (backend decides).\n */\nconst DEFAULT_EFFORT_LADDER: readonly string[] = ['low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh']\n\n/** Selectable reasoning effort as dsh-llm's resolveModel contract describes it. */\nexport interface ZenReasoningEffort {\n  id: string\n  name: string\n  description?: string\n}\n\n/**\n * Turn the catalog's models.dev capability into the advertised effort list.\n * A declared ladder (models.dev `reasoning_options` effort values) wins — its\n * values are the upstream-honored spellings, with metadata `none` folded into\n * our `off`. inbounds, pool proxies) and let the relay walk\n// them instead of pinning one.\nconst proxyList = (process.env.DSH_ZEN_PROXIES || process.env.DSH_ZEN_PROXY || '')\n  .split(/[,\\\\s]+/).map((p) => p.trim()).filter(Boolean)\n// A proxy that just failed is benched, not banned: v2rayN switches node several\n// times an hour and the SAME inbound becomes usable again seconds later.\nconst cooldownMs Map()\nlet cursor = 0\n\nfunction candidates() {\n  const now = Date.now()\n  const ready = []\n  for (let i = 0; i < proxyList.length; i++) {\n    const p = proxyList[(cursor + i) % relay's own hop-by-hop headers must not leak to the Node side, and a\n  // dropped content-encoding invalidates the upstream content-length.\n  out.delete('content-encoding')\n  out.delete('content-length')\n  out.delete('transfer-encoding')\n  out.delete('connection')\n  return new Response(res.body, { status: res.status, statusText: res.statusText, headers: out })\n}\n\nfunction relayError(status, message) {\n  return new Response(JSON.stringify({ type: 'error', error: { type: 'RelayError', message } }), {\n    status,\n    headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },\n  })\n}\n\nconst server = Bun.serve({\n  hostname: '127.0.0.1',\n  port: 0,\n  idleTimeout: 255,\n  async fetch(req) {\n    const url = new URL(req.url)\n    const target = }\n    if (keepAlive) init.keepalive = true\n    let payload\n    if (req.method !== 'GET' && req.method !== 'HEAD') {\n      // Read once: a retry through the next exit must send the same bytes.\n      payload = await req.arrayBuffer()\n      init.body = payload\n    }\n\n    // Order: usable exits in rotation order, then direct (unless forbidden).\n    const order = candidates()\n    if res = await (proxy ? fetch(target, { ...init, proxy }) : fetch(target, init))\n      } catch (err) {\n        lastError = err\n        if (proxy) { bench(proxy, err && err.code ? err.code : 'connect failed'); continue }\n        console.error('direct exit failed: ' + (err && err.message ? err.message : err))\n        continue\n      }\n      if (res.status === 429 && rest > 0) {\n        // 429 'where' : 'which'\n  try {\n    const out = execFileSync(probe, ['bun'], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 5000, stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore'] })\n    const found = out.split(/\\r?\\n/).map((line) => line.trim()).filter((line) => line.length > 0 && existsSync(line))\n    // On Windows `where bun` also lists the extension-less sh shim, which is\n    // not executable through spawn(): prefer the real binary, then the .cmd.\n    const executable = found.find((line) => /\\.exe$/i.test(line))\n      ?? found.find((line) => /\\.cmd$/i.test(line))\n      ?? found.find((line) => process.platform !== 'win32' || /\\.(bat|ps1)$/i.test(line))\n    if (executable) return executable\n  } catch {\n    // not on PATH\n  }\n  for (const guess of [\n    join(process.env.LOCALAPPDATA ?? '', '.bun', 'bin', 'bun.exe'),\n    '/usr/local/bin/bun',\n    '/opt/homebrew/bin/bun',\n  ]) {\n    if (guess.length > 0 && existsSync(guess)) return guess\n  }\n  return null\n}\n\nfunction scriptPath(dir: string | undefined): string {\n  const target = dir ?? join(tmpdir(), 'dsh-plugin-adapter')\n  mkdirSync(target, { recursive: true })\n  const file = join(target, 'zen-relay.mjs')\n  writeFileSync(file, RELAY_SCRIPT, 'utf8')\n  return file\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the relay handle. Returns null when bun cannot be found, so the caller\n * can keep its previous transport untouched.\n */\nexport function createZenRelay(options: ZenRelayOptions = {}): ZenRelay | null {\n  const bun = resolveBunPath(options.bunPath)\n  if (bun === null) return null\n  /** Narrowed copy for closures (TS forgets the guard inside them). */\n  const bunBin: string = bun\n\n  const upstream = (options.upstream ?? [options.proxyUrl] : []))\n    .map((url) => url.trim())\n    .filter((url) => url.length > 0)\n  // Loopback traffic must never ride the ambient proxy dispatcher.\n  const loopback = new Agent({ connections: 32, pipelining: 0 })\n\n  let child: ChildProcessByStdio<null, Readable, Readable> | null = null\n  let port = 0\n  let starting: Promise<boolean> | null = null\n  let disposed = false\n  let attempts = 0\n\n  const log = options.log ??       "content": "/**\n * ip-pool settings controller — glues the settings namespace (docs/ip-pool.md\n * §5.1) to the runtime assembly (ip-pool.ts) with live apply, and mounts the\n * status/probe bridge (§5.3) on the host webServer.\n *\n * Lifecycle (all no-restart, docs §7 IP-5 acceptance):\n *  - entry config enabled at boot: pool assembles immediately;\n *  - namespace registers with the composition entry as `base`, applies live;\n *  - watch(next) hot-applies every commit through runtime.reconfigure() —\n *    including the `enabled` flip (dispatcher install/uninstall) and address\n *    list edits (manual rows rebuilt, pinned re-pinned);\n *  - bridge routes mount once the webServer service shows up (ctx.inject),\n *    reading the live runtime and the current settings value.\n */\n\nimport type { PluginContext } from '../index.ts'\nimport type { DshPluginAdapterConfig } from '../config.ts'\nimport type { IpPoolRuntime } from '../ip-pool.ts'\nimport { IP_POOL_NAMESPACE, IpPoolConfigSchema, toIpPoolConfig, type IpPoolSettings } from './namespace.ts'\nimport { IP_POOL_BRIDGE_PREFIX, makeBridgeHandlers, makeBridgeRoutes } from './bridge.ts'\n\n/** Either layer's ip-pool section (settings value or plugin config shape). */\ntype AnyIpPoolSection = Partial<IpPoolSettings> & {\n  subscriptions?: string[]\n  free?: Partial<IpPoolSettings['free']>\n  subscription?: Partial<IpPoolSettings['subscription']>\n}\n\n/** Extract the ip-pool settings value with defaults filled (schema-independent). */\nfunction withDefaults(value: AnyIpPoolSection | undefined): IpPoolSettings {\n  const raw = value ?? {}\n  const urls = raw.subscription?.urls ?? raw.subscriptions ?? []\n  return {\n    enabled: raw.enabled ?? false,\n    probeModels: raw.probeModels ?? [],\n    maxConcurrentProbes: raw.maxConcurrentProbes ?? 3,\n    free: {\n      enabled: raw.free?.enabled ?? true,\n      targetSize: raw.free?.targetSize ?? 20,\n      blockedCountries: raw.free?.blockedCountries ?? ['CN'],\n    },\n    manual: raw.manual ?? [],\n    subscription: {\n      urls,\n      refreshMs: raw.subscription?.refreshMs ?? 30 * 60_000,\n    },\n    singbox: { path: raw.singbox?.path ?? 'sing-box' },\n    pinnedExitId: raw.pinnedExitId ?? '',\n    pinnedStrict: raw.pinnedStrict ?? false,\n    proxyHosts: raw.proxyHosts ??       "path": "packages/plugin/src/pool/installer.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * Installer — global-dispatcher install/swap/restore (docs/ip-pool.md 2, the\n * makeInstaller pattern from dsh-llm-proxy, adapted):\n *\n *  - installs a PoolRoutingDispatcher only while routing is enabled;\n *  - remembers the pre-existing dispatcher and restores it on disable and\n *    on plugin dispose (another dispatcher plugin — e.g. dsh-llm-proxy —\n *    must not stay short-circuited by us);\n *  - disables by restoring + destroying ours.\n *\n * The rotate-retry loop (3.4) is intentionally NOT here: this layer only\n * routes; the adapter-level loop owns failure semantics.\n */\n\nimport type { Dispatcher } from 'undici'\n\nimport { PoolRoutingDispatcher, type RoutingDispatcherSurface, type UndiciSeam } from './dispatcher.ts'\nimport type { ExitPool } from './pool.ts'\n\n/** The setter accepts the full Dispatcher; our router exposes the subset\n *  fetch exercises (RoutingDispatcherSurface — same duck-typing contract\n *  dsh-llm-proxy validated on this host). */\ntype InstallableDispatcher = Parameters<UndiciSeam['setGlobalDispatcher']>[0]\n\nexport interface InstallerDeps {\n  pool: ExitPool\n  undici: UndiciSeam\n  proxyHosts?: string[]\n  logger?: { info(message: string): void; warn(message: string): void }\n}\n\n/**\n * Why the routing layer is not active (docs/ip-pool.md R1, coexistence\n * policy): another dispatcher-level plugin owns the global dispatcher, so we\n * deferred instead of short-circuiting it. Null = routing is active.\n */\nexport type DeferredReason = string | null\n\nexport class RoutingInstaller {\n  #deps: InstallerDeps\n  #previous: Dispatcher | null = null\n  #current: PoolRoutingDispatcher | null = null\n  #enabled = false\n  #deferredReason: DeferredReason = null\n  /** The built-in fetch saved aside while the module fetch is installed (R2). */\n  #savedGlobalFetch: unknown = null\n\n  constructor(deps: InstallerDeps) {\n    this.#deps = deps\n  }\n\n  get enabled(): boolean {\n    return this.#enabled\n  }\n\n  /** The deferral reason exposed to the status bridge / settings card. */\n  get deferredReason(): DeferredReason {\n    return this.#deferredReason\n  }\n\n  /** Live re-apply of the proxied-host list (forwards to the running router). */\n  setProxyHosts(hosts?: string[]): void {\n    this.#deps.proxyHosts = hosts\n    this.#current?.setProxyHosts(hosts)\n  }\n\n  /**\n   * Decide whether installing is safe (docs/ip-pool.md R1 coexistence policy).\n   * The global dispatcher slot is single-owner: if another dispatcher-level\n   * plugin (dsh-llm-proxy etc.) already installed its own layer, installing\n   * ours would short-circuit theirs silently. We defer instead — routing\n   * stays off, the pool keeps assembling (exits/probes/settings all live),\n   * and the reason surfaces on the settings card. Default Agent instances\n   * (undici's own) are not treated as a foreign owner.\n   */\n  #detectForeignDispatcher(): DeferredReason | null {\n    let current: unknown\n    try {\n      current = this.#deps.undici.getGlobalDispatcher()\n    } catch {\n      return null\n    }\n    if (current === null || current === undefined) return null\n    const foreign = current as { constructor?: { name?: string } }\n    const name = foreign.constructor?.name ?? ''\n    // undici's own defaults, plain-object stand-ins (tests, hosts that never\n    // installed anything), and anything unnamed are not a foreign plugin.\n    if (name === '' || name === 'Object' || name === 'Agent' || name === 'Dispatcher') return null\n    if (current instanceof (this.#deps.undici.Agent as unknown as { new (): unknown })) return null\n    return `deferred: global dispatcher is owned by \"${name}\" — install dsh-llm-proxy or the IP pool in one profile only, not both (R1)`\n  }\n\n  /** Install (or keep installed) the routing dispatcher. */\n  install(): void {\n    if (this.#enabled) return\n    const foreign = this.#detectForeignDispatcher()\n    if (foreign !== null) {\n      this.#deferredReason = foreign\n      this.#deps.logger?.warn(`dsh-plugin-adapter: exit routing ${foreign}`)\n      return\n    }\n    this.#deferredReason = null\n    const router = new PoolRoutingDispatcher({\n      pool: this.#deps.pool,\n      undici: this.#deps.undici,\n      proxyHosts: this.#deps.proxyHosts,\n      logger: this.#deps.logger,\n    })\n    const previous = this.#deps.undici.setGlobalDispatcher(router as unknown as InstallableDispatcher)\n    // undici's setter returns the replaced dispatcher (void on some hosts)\n    if (previous instanceof Object) this.#previous = previous as Dispatcher\n    const old = this.#current\n    this.#current = router\n    this.#enabled = true\n    if (old !== null) void old.destroy().catch(() => {})\n    // Global-fetch capture (R2, live-observed 2026-09-09): Node's built-in\n    // fetch reads the BUILT-IN undici's dispatcher slot — a different module\n    // instance than the npm undici this seam routes through — so\n    // setGlobalDispatcher alone never routes the OpenAI SDK's requests\n    // (it captures globalThis.fetch at call time). Swap the global fetch to\n    // the module's own (which honors OUR dispatcher slot) while routing is\n    // enabled; restore on disable. Only when the module actually exposes a\n    // distinct fetch — a same-instance host needs nothing.\n    const moduleFetch = this.#deps.undici.fetch\n    if (typeof moduleFetch === 'function' && globalThis.fetch !== moduleFetch) {\n      this.#savedGlobalFetch = globalThis.fetch\n      ;(globalThis as { fetch: unknown }).fetch = moduleFetch\n      this.#deps.logger?.info('dsh-plugin-adapter: globalThis.fetch -> undici module fetch (built-in fetch bypasses the pool dispatcher otherwise)')\n    }\n    this.#deps.logger?.info('dsh-plugin-adapter: global dispatcher -> PoolRoutingDispatcher (exit routing enabled)')\n  }\n\n  /** Restore the pre-install dispatcher and close ours. */\n  disable(): void {\n    if (!this.#enabled) return\n    this.#enabled = false\n    if (this.#savedGlobalFetch !== null) {\n      ;(globalThis as { fetch: unknown }).fetch = this.#savedGlobalFetch\n      this.#savedGlobalFetch = null\n    }\n    if (this.#previous !== null) {\n      try {\n        this.#deps.undici.setGlobalDispatcher(this.#previous)\n      } catch {\n        // the saved dispatcher may already be gone (host teardown) — our\n        // uninstall still succeeded for our own layer\n      }\n      this.#previous = null\n    }\n    const dying = this.#current\n    this.#current = null\n    if (dying !== null) void dying.destroy().catch(() => {})\n    this.#deps.logger?.info('dsh-plugin-adapter: exit routing disabled; previous global dispatcher restored')\n  }\n\n  /** Full teardown (plugin dispose): same as disable. */\n  dispose(): void {\n    this.disable()\n  }\n}\n"
    },

      "path": "packages/plugin/src/provider.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * Registers the local agent into DSH's llm-pi-ai provider settings and keeps\n * the model list fresh (plan.md 1.5, per Appendix A conclusion).\n *\n * Two touches, both idempotent:\n *  1. credentials: store the local token behind apiKeyEnv so the settings\n *     document never carries the secret (ctx.credentials.set).\n *  2. settings: ensure llm-pi-ai.providers.<providerId> exists with baseURL\n *     http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1 and the model list from GET /v1/models\n *     (ctx.settings.mutate on the user section).\n */\n\nexport interface AgentModel {\n  id: string\n  name?: string\n  description?: string\n}\n\nexport interface PiAiModelEntry {\n  id: string\n  name: string\n}\n\nexport interface ProviderTarget {\n  providerId: string\n  apiKeyEnv: string\n  port: number\n}\n\nexport function providerBaseURL(port: number): string {\n  return `http://127.0.0.1:${port}/v1`\n}\n\n/**\n * Remove the llm-pi-ai provider route left behind by sidecar mode. Adapter\n * mode serves the provider id itself; a stale route pointing at a dead\n * sidecar port would shadow dispatch and fail every call with a connection\n * error. Returns true when a route was actually removed.\n *\n * `extraProviderIds` carries the pre-0.4.0 route name: a sidecar install\n * from the old era still has `providers.opencode2dsh` in the host settings,\n * and that leftover would shadow the adapter exactly like the current id.\n */\nexport async function removeProviderRoute(\n  seams: Pick<DshSeams, 'settings'>,\n  providerId: string,\n  extraProviderIds: readonly string[] = [],\n): Promise<boolean> {\n  const namespace = seams.settings.get('llm-pi-ai') as { providers?: Record<string, unknown> } | undefined\n  if (!namespace?.providers) return false\n  const stale = [providerId, ...extraProviderIds].filter((id) => id in namespace.providers!)\n  if (stale.length === 0) return false\n  await seams.settings.mutate(\n    'llm-pi-ai',\n    stale.map((id) => ({ op: 'unset' as const, path: ['providers', id] })),\n  )\n  return true\n}\n\n/** Minimal settings/credentials seam so tests can run against fakes. */\nexport interface DshSeams {\n  credentials: {\n    set(ref: string, value: string): Promise<void>\n  }\n  settings: {\n    get(ns: string): unknown\n    mutate(ns: string, ops: Array<{ op: 'set' | 'unset'; path: Array<string | number>; value?: unknown }>): Promise<void>\n  }\n  logger: { info(message: string): void; warn(message: string): void }\n}\n\n/** Parse the agent's OpenAI-shaped /v1/models reply into pi-ai model entries. */\nexport function toPiAiModels(data: unknown): PiAiModelEntry[] {\n  if (!data || typeof data !== 'object') return []\n  const list = (data as { data?: unknown }).data\n  if (!Array.isArray(list)) return []\n  const seen = new Set<string>()\n  const entries: PiAiModelEntry[] = []\n  for (const item of list) {\n    if (!item || typeof item !== 'object') continue\n    const id = (item as { id?: unknown }).id\n    if (typeof id !== 'string' || id.length === 0 || seen.has(id)) continue\n    seen.add(id)\n    const name = (item as { name?: unknown }).name\n    entries.push({\n      id,\n      name: typeof name === 'string' && name.length > 0 ? name : id,\n    })\n  }\n  return entries\n}\n\nexport async function fetchModels(port: number, token: string, timeoutMs = 10000): Promise<PiAiModelEntry[]> {\n  const controller = new AbortController()\n  const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), timeoutMs)\n  try {\n    const response = await fetch(providerBaseURL(port) + '/models', {\n      headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },\n      signal: controller.signal,\n    })\n    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`GET /v1/models failed: HTTP ${response.status}`)\n    return toPiAiModels(await response.json())\n  } finally {\n    clearTimeout(timer)\n  }\n}\n\n/** GET /healthz (no auth); throws on transport failure or non-2xx. */\nexport async function fetchHealth(port: number, timeoutMs = 3000): Promise<unknown> {\n  const controller = new AbortController()\n  const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), timeoutMs)\n  try {\n    const response = await fetch(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}/healthz`, { signal: controller.signal })\n    if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`GET /healthz failed: HTTP ${response.status}`)\n    return await response.json()\n  } finally {\n    clearTimeout(timer)\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Ensure the credential and the llm-pi-ai provider route reflect the running\n * agent. Safe to call repeatedly (every refresh): writes are no-ops when the\n * stored shape already matches, and mutate keeps other namespaces/routes\n * untouched because it edits only the dsh-plugin-adapter subtree.\n */\nexport async function registerProvider(\n  seams: DshSeams,\n  target: ProviderTarget,\n  token: string,\n  models: PiAiModelEntry[],\n): Promise<void> {\n  await seams.credentials.set(target.apiKeyEnv, token)\n\n  const route = {\n    displayName: 'dsh-plugin-adapter',\n    apiKeyEnv: target.apiKeyEnv,\n    api: 'openai-completions',\n    baseURL: providerBaseURL(target.port),\n    models,\n  }\n  await seams.settings.mutate('llm-pi-ai', [\n    { op: 'set', path: ['providers', target.providerId], value: route },\n  ])\n  seams.logger.info(`dsh-plugin-adapter: registered llm-pi-ai provider \"${target.providerId}\" with ${models.length} model(s) at ${route.baseURL}`)\n}\n"
    }
  ],
